preamble: Vocalization of the voiced dental fricative [ð] to the labio-velar glide [w] in syllable-final position. It is a hallmark of early Old Catalan: Latin intervocalic -d- had lenited to [ð], and where loss of the following vowel left it word-final, or syncope placed it before a consonant, it vocalized to [w] (PEDEM > peu [ˈpɛw], NIDUM > niu, CREDERE > creure). Recasens links the change to the retracted tongue-dorsum posture of open Catalan [ð].

examples.note: Word-final [ð], left final by loss of the Latin final vowel, vocalized to [w]; the change is cited by Recasens for this word.
Not to be confused with creu 'cross' < crucem, whose [w] comes from the affricate /dz/.
Before a consonant created by syncope, [ð] vocalized as it did word-finally.

sources: Recasens, D. (2014). Fonètica i fonologia experimentals del català. Vocals i consonants. Barcelona: Institut d'Estudis Catalans. https://publicacions.iec.cat/repository/pdf/00000333/00000023.pdf
